name: Gordon Ryan Side Control to North-South System
description: Navigate Gordon Ryan’s side-control and north-south course by escape concern or arm-isolation goal, with a focused comparison to Danaher’s side crucifix.
summary: Separate side-control retention, arm isolation and north-south transitions in Gordon Ryan’s top-pins curriculum.
overview: Systematically attacking From Top Pins: Side Control & North South by Gordon Ryan treats retention, limb isolation and changes between pins as distinct study topics. The outline includes near- and far-arm sections alongside north-south maintenance, so a failed attack and a lost pin need not lead to the same lesson.

fits: You can reach side control but need to identify whether your next study concerns retention, arm isolation or changing pins.

includes: Side-control escape responses and separate near- and far-arm isolation sections.
Movement to north-south and responses to knee recovery or turning.
Submission branches plus rolling and commentary volumes.

start_here.title: Choose retention or relocation before choosing a submission
start_here.task: Compare Volume 2’s knee/elbow-connection topics with Volume 5’s north-south movement and knee-recovery topics in the public outline. Place your current question under staying in side control or changing pins. If you have access, begin with Why and When to Move to North South and note the stated reason for changing position before watching an attack branch.
